IsDeterministic.maps_to: CrystalSphere.cs:34 `IsDeterministic => false` overrides EventModel.cs's `!IsShared`. Its ONLY consumer is EventRoom.Exit (EventRoom.cs), which emits a multiplayer desync CHECKSUM when the event is deterministic and skips it when it is not; nothing reads it on a gameplay path. The sim has no IsDeterministic surface and needs none -- it has no checksum tracker. NOTE the prior reasoning here ('this unit's CalculateVars is unreachable behind is_allowed') died with the stub: calculate_vars runs on every visit now, and the verdict stands on the checksum-only consumer instead.

CalculateVars.maps_to: CrystalSphere.calculate_vars (events/crystal_sphere.py:66-71) is `cost = 50 + event_rng.next_int_range(1, 50)`, C#'s `base.DynamicVars["UncoverFutureCost"].BaseValue += base.Rng.NextInt(1, 50)` (CrystalSphere.cs:44-47) over the 50m canonical base (:38). `Rng.NextInt(minInclusive, maxExclusive)` (Rng.cs) makes the roll 1..49 and `Rng.next_int_range` (sts2_rl/rng.py) is the same half-open range, taken on the event's own stream rather than the shared run rng. Reached from Event.begin (events/base.py:172).
CalculateVars.issue: Closed 2026-08-03. The dormancy this entry recorded was entirely a consequence of the IsAllowed stub, and the stub is gone: the roll now happens on every visit, and the cost it produces is what UNCOVER_FUTURE charges. EXECUTED: test/test_crystal_sphere.py::test_uncover_future_costs_50_plus_a_1_to_49_roll drives the event and asserts the charge is 50 + a 1..49 draw off the event rng; the trigger this entry named ('fixing IsAllowed is what would make this live -- at that point the NextInt(1,50) roll would need a sim counterpart too') is exactly what landed, and the counterpart landed with it.

IsAllowed.issue: Closed 2026-08-03. RE-EXECUTED THIS ENTRY'S OWN WITNESS: `.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/misc-crystal-sphere-witness.py` (act_index = 1, gold = 250) now prints `CrystalSphere.is_allowed(run): True` and `crystal_sphere in allowed_events(SHARED_EVENTS)? True`, then trips its own `assert CrystalSphere.is_allowed(run) is False, "gate still hard-False"` -- the witness fails in the opposite direction, which is the strongest form of close this pipeline has. The blocker this entry recorded was CORRECT and is why the gate did not land alone: RoomSet.ensure_next_event_is_valid (sts2_rl/rooms.py) applies is_allowed as the SOLE routing gate with no options-emptiness fallback, and Event.begin()/_set_state (events/base.py:167-176, 319-323) silently self-finishes an empty-options event, so a gate without a body would have traded one divergence for another. That reasoning is now pinned by test/test_r14_events_ports.py::test_crystal_sphere_routing_has_no_fallback_for_an_empty_bodied_event. The gate and the body landed together; see guard 1.

guards.maps_to: The minigame is ported in events/_crystal_sphere.py -- the 11x11 grid, the radius-2 corner pre-clear, the 15 items built in the source's construction order with one `NextItem` placement draw each (including the `&&` short-circuit and the 10-try retry loop, CrystalSphereMinigame.cs:126-134), the Big/Small clear shapes in the source's neighbour order, and the all-cells-clear reveal rule -- and driven from CrystalSphere._play (events/crystal_sphere.py:95-112), which spends one divination per click whatever the tool. The two arms match CrystalSphere.cs:67-81: UNCOVER_FUTURE loses `50 + roll` gold and drives 3 divinations, PAYMENT_PLAN adds a Debt curse and drives 6. The payout is _grant (:135-194), reveal-ordered.
guards.issue: Closed 2026-08-03. THE PREMISE WAS FALSE ON BOTH HALVES, and neither half was refuted by argument -- both were refuted by files nobody had searched. (a) 'no headless analogue for a 121-cell spatial choice': the source ships one. CrystalSphereScreenHandler.cs:82-104 is the game's OWN automated player for this screen and clicks `random.NextItem(cells where c.Visible && c.Entity.IsHidden)`. The workaround is therefore to play the minigame randomly by exactly that rule: CrystalSphere._default_click (events/crystal_sphere.py:114-123) picks a uniformly random still-hidden cell and clicks it with the tool the ctor selects (CrystalSphereMinigame.cs:134 `CrystalSphereTool = CrystalSphereToolType.Big`) -- a cited rule, not an invented one. The click draw comes off a SIM-ONLY `RunState.crystal_sphere_rng`, because the game spends no run RNG on a human click and drawing from any parity stream would shift every later placement and reward draw; pinned by test_crystal_sphere.py::test_clicking_never_touches_a_parity_rng_stream. (b) 'a replay needs a policy': it does not. RunReplays already records the decision verbatim as `CrystalSphereClick {x} {y} {tool}` (the RunReplays repo's Commands/CrystalSphereClickCommand, with Patches/CrystalSpherePatch), and `run.crystal_sphere_clicks` feeds those recorded clicks straight into the engine, the random rule taking over only where the recording has none left; pinned by test_a_recorded_click_list_drives_the_minigame_exactly. What the old text got RIGHT: landing LoseGold/AddCurseToDeck without the minigame would have made the player pay for nothing, so gate and body landed together. DELIBERATELY NOT MODELLED: the cell click as an RL *action* -- a 121-wide block does not fit CHOICE_SLOTS and at this event's frequency such a head would never train; the two EVENT options are surfaced normally. 37 tests in test/test_crystal_sphere.py cover grid construction, placement draw counts, both tools, reveal semantics, both arms and the payout.

guards.what: the relic pull and each card group's populate must run in REVEAL order, the way C# populates one ordered reward list
guards.maps_to: C# hands the revealed items to `RewardsCmd.OfferCustom`, so they enter `RewardsSet.Rewards` through WithCustomRewards (RewardsSet.cs:106-110) and are populated by the FIRST loop of GenerateWithoutOffering (`foreach (Reward reward in Rewards) reward.Populate();`, RewardsSet.cs:130-134) -- in list order, i.e. reveal order, and BEFORE Hook.ModifyRewards; only rewards a hook ADDED populate afterwards (`Rewards.Except(second)`, :136-142). `CrystalSphere._grant` (events/crystal_sphere.py:135-207) is now the same two passes: pass 1 builds one row per revealed item in reveal order (the potion being the only kind that rolls there, CrystalSpherePotion.cs:31-38) and records the reveal order that `CombatRewards`'s separate card/relic collections cannot carry; pass 2 walks that order populating each row -- a card group draws its three options, a relic reward pulls from the grab bag on the event's own rng -- and only then does `apply_reward_modifiers` (sts2_rl/rewards.py) run the two ModifyRewards passes and the Except-sweep. The take-or-skip screen (`run.offer_relic`) stays AFTER the hooks, because RelicReward.Populate is the pull and RelicReward.OnSelect is the obtain (RelicReward.cs:74-91, 109-123): a declined relic has still left the bag.
guards.issue: Filed and closed 2026-08-03. FILED because the port's own module docstring named a residual no entry carried -- the relic pull was hoisted behind every card group's populate, so on the event's own rng the sim's order was [potion rolls] [card options] [relic pull] where the game's is plain reveal order, and a relic revealed before a card item changed both the relic and the cards. REACHABILITY, executed before the fix: under the sim's automated click rule (uniform hidden cell, Big tool) over 20,000 boards per arm a relic and a card item are never revealed together at 3 divinations (0/20,000) and are in 34/20,000 (0.17%) at 6, relic first in 4 of those -- but under a TARGETED click list, which is what a recorded human run is, relic-before-card is the ordinary case: digging the relic first then spending what is left on cards produced it on all 12 seeds tried. CLOSED by the two-pass rewrite described in maps_to. Pinned by test/test_crystal_sphere.py::test_the_relic_pulls_at_its_reveal_position_not_after_the_card_sweep, which spies on RunState.pull_relic_from_front and CardRewardGroup.populate and asserts the call order equals the reveal order; it failed `['card', 'card', 'relic'] != ['relic', 'card', 'card']` before the change. Full suite 4527 passed / 6 xfailed.
